meta.name: Rebook disrupted flights and notify passengers with Claude, Google Sheets, and Twilio

name: Rebook passengers automatically after flight cancellations or delays

parameters.content:
## IROPS Auto-Rebooking Agent

This workflow continuously polls live flight status against active bookings, detects Irregular Operations (IROPS) events (cancellations and severe delays), uses AI to pick the best alternative flight per passenger and draft a calm, personal notification, writes every rebooking decision to a log, and texts the passenger before they ever have to call.

### Who's it for
- Airlines and OTAs that want autonomous rebooking instead of call-center queues during IROPS
- Corporate travel desks monitoring VIP/loyalty travelers across many flights
- Travel agencies that need to proactively protect client itineraries
- Anyone who wants passengers rebooked and notified in minutes, not hours

### How it works
1. A schedule trigger polls a live flight-status feed and the active bookings list (both modeled as Google Sheets, swap for a real GDS/airline ops API)
2. Flight status is matched against each active booking to compute an impact level: On Time, Minor Delay, Severe Delay, or Cancelled
3. Every booking's status is logged to the OpsLog tab on every run, building a continuous IROPS audit trail regardless of impact
4. Bookings that are Cancelled or Severely Delayed are filtered out for rebooking action
5. Alternate flight inventory on the same route is fetched and narrowed to seats-available options in the passenger's cabin class
6. AI selects the best alternative (or explains why none exists yet) and writes a short, calm SMS notification plus the rebooking reason
7. The rebooking decision is appended to the Rebookings log tab
8. The passenger receives an SMS confirming their new flight before they need to call in

### How to set up
1. Import this workflow into n8n
2. Add Anthropic Claude credentials and attach to the Anthropic model node
3. Add Twilio credentials (HTTP Basic Auth, using your Twilio Account SID and Auth Token) and attach them to the Send SMS node; replace YOUR_TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID and YOUR_TWILIO_PHONE_NUMBER
4. Switch the Google Sheets HTTP nodes to the native Google Sheets node with OAuth2, or add OAuth2 credentials directly
5. Replace YOUR_SHEET_ID in all Sheets HTTP nodes with your actual Spreadsheet ID
6. Set up your Google Sheet with five tabs: FlightStatus, Bookings, Inventory, OpsLog, Rebookings (column layouts below)
7. Set the schedule interval to match how often your flight-status feed updates (default: every 5 minutes)
8. Activate the workflow

### Requirements
- Anthropic Claude API key (claude-sonnet-4 recommended)
- Twilio account for SMS delivery
- Google Sheets with OAuth2 credentials (FlightStatus, Bookings, Inventory, OpsLog, Rebookings tabs)

### How to customize
- Adjust the delay thresholds that define Minor vs Severe delay in JS - Match Bookings & Detect IROPS Impact
- Add loyalty-tier priority ordering so top-tier travelers get first pick of scarce alternative seats
- Add an email node alongside SMS for passengers who prefer email, or a Slack node for the ops desk
- Replace the FlightStatus and Inventory Sheets fetches with a real GDS/airline ops API (e.g. AeroAPI, Sabre, Amadeus)
- Add a human-approval step (e.g. Slack Approve/Deny) before the SMS goes out for VIP or high-fare bookings

### Google Sheets column layout

FlightStatus tab - row 1 headers:
Flight Number | Origin | Destination | Scheduled Departure | Status | Delay Minutes | Aircraft | Last Updated

Bookings tab - row 1 headers:
Booking ID | Passenger Name | Phone | Email | Flight Number | Cabin Class | Loyalty Tier | Seat | Status

Inventory tab - row 1 headers:
Flight Number | Origin | Destination | Departure Time | Arrival Time | Seats Available | Cabin Classes Available

OpsLog tab - row 1 headers:
Checked At | Booking ID | Passenger Name | Flight Number | Flight Status | Delay Minutes | Impact Level | Origin | Destination

Rebookings tab - row 1 headers:
Rebooked At | Booking ID | Passenger Name | Original Flight | New Flight | New Departure | Reason | Alternative Offered

## Stage 1: Data Collection & IROPS Matching

Schedule Trigger polls on a fixed interval (default every 5 minutes). Two parallel fetches pull the latest FlightStatus feed and the currently active Bookings list.

Each fetch is followed by a small JS node that renames the raw Sheets `values` array so the two datasets don't collide once merged.

Merge - Combine Status & Bookings joins both datasets into a single item by position.

JS - Match Bookings & Detect IROPS Impact builds one object per active booking: its matched flight status, delay minutes, and an impactLevel (On Time / Minor Delay / Severe Delay / Cancelled).

Split Out - Bookings turns that single array into one item per booking so the rest of the workflow can process each passenger independently.

## Stage 2: Continuous Ops Log

This branch runs for every booking on every cycle, regardless of impact level - it's what builds the continuous IROPS audit trail.

JS - Format Ops Log Record assembles the row for the OpsLog tab: timestamp, flight status, delay minutes, and impact level.

Save Booking Status to Google Sheets OpsLog appends that row, so the sheet always reflects the latest state across every active booking.

## Stage 3: AI Rebooking Decision

Filter - Cancelled or Severe Delay Only lets through only bookings whose flight was cancelled or delayed 120+ minutes, so on-time and mildly delayed passengers never trigger AI calls or rebookings.

A Wait buffer respects API rate limits, then Fetch Alternate Flight Inventory pulls the full route inventory and JS - Filter Inventory for Matching Route narrows it to same-route options with available seats in the passenger's cabin class, sorted by departure time.

The rebooking AI (claude-sonnet-4, temperature 0.2 for consistent decisions) picks the best alternative flight, explains the reason, and writes a short SMS-ready notification.

JS - Parse Rebooking Output extracts the structured JSON safely, with a fallback that auto-selects the earliest available candidate flight (or explains that none exist yet) if AI parsing fails.

## Stage 4: Rebooking Log & Notification

JS - Format Rebooking Log Record assembles the row for the Rebookings tab: original flight, new flight, new departure time, reason, and whether an alternative was offered.

Write Rebooking to Google Sheets Log appends that row, keeping a permanent record of every autonomous rebooking decision.

Send SMS Alert to Passenger delivers the new flight details and reason to the passenger's phone via Twilio - reaching them before they ever have to call in.
